title: Fake Apple runtime for host tests (CoreFoundation / CoreMedia / CoreVideo / VideoToolbox subset)
done: fake/fake_apple.c implements every function and constant declared in include/n2_apple.h: refcounted, type-tagged CF objects; CFRelease at 0 frees; long n2fake_live_objects() counts live releasable objects (atomic); interned strings and the static singletons are process lifetime and exempt.

CFString: n2fake_cfstr interns by content (same text -> same pointer, including the declared key constants); CFStringCreateWithCString creates a counted copy; CFStringGetCString bounds-checks the destination.

CFDictionary: insertion-ordered (key,value) array; keys compared with CFEqual (strings by content, numbers by value, others by pointer); retains keys and values; overwrite replaces the value and keeps the existing key object (Apple CFDictionary behaviour); CFArray equally insertion-ordered and retaining.
CFNumber stores int64 for SInt32/SInt64 and double for Float64; CFNumberGetValue converts with range checks (NaN and out-of-range return false).
CMBlockBuffer: borrowed block (caller memory) or owned zeroed malloc block when memoryBlock==NULL; Replace/Copy are bounds-checked against the data area and return -12704; CMBlockBufferGetDataLength.

CMSampleBufferCreateReady retains the block buffer and format description, keeps timing[0] and a copy of the sample-size array; sample attachments array is created on demand with one mutable dictionary per sample; NotSync/DependsOnOthers keys are the declared constants.

CMVideoFormatDescriptionCreateFromH264ParameterSets copies the parameter sets and rejects count<2, NAL header length not 1/2/4, and a first NAL whose nal_unit_type is not 7 with -12712; GetH264ParameterSetAtIndex returns the copies, count and NAL length.

CVPixelBuffer: 420v/420f (two planes, luma and interleaved chroma stride = width rounded up to 64) and i420 (three planes, chroma stride = round64(ceil(width/2))); Lock/Unlock counted; GetBaseAddressOfPlane returns NULL while unlocked; plane height/bytes-used/data-size inspectors.

fake/fake_vt.c: CMDerivedObjectCreate allocates the object plus zero-filled derivedStorageSize bytes, stores the n2_VTVideoEncoderVTable, returns -12780 for any class id other than VTVideoEncoderGetClassID(); CMBaseObjectGetDerivedStorage; VTVideoEncoderGetCMBaseObject is the identity; releasing the object calls baseClass->finalize exactly once.
VTRegisterVideoEncoder/VTRegisterVideoEncoderWithInfo append to a mutex-protected registry readable by n2fake_vt_registered; n2fake_vt_reset releases retained info dictionaries.

n2fake_session_* drives an encoder exactly as specified: create (createInstance then startSession), encode with a fresh frame token and local CMTime copies, complete, set/copy property through baseClass, emitted records with borrowed sample buffers, pixel attributes, vtable/encoder accessors, sticky protocol-error counter, destroy (releases encoder -> finalize once, sample buffers and attributes).

VTEncoderSessionEmitEncodedFrame retains the sample buffer and validates the frame token: a second emit for one token or a token never submitted increments n2fake_session_protocol_errors and still records the emit.
The fake aborts with a message naming the function on NULL where real CoreFoundation would crash; CFRelease(NULL) is the one documented NULL-safe call.

gpu/video/fake/test/t_fake.c: 10 test functions with literal expectations covering strings/numbers/booleans, dictionary order/overwrite/retain counts, array, block-buffer bounds, sample timing/attachments, H.264 SPS/PPS round trip and rejections, 178x146 plane layout, a toy 64-byte-derived-storage encoder through the session driver (emit count, token matching, finalize once, double/unknown emit), concurrent use of the intern table/refcounts/live counter, and address-taking of every declared symbol.
gpu/video/fake/run_tests.sh builds into gpu/video/build/WP02 by default with ASan+UBSan (-Werror), runs the suite, then rebuilds and reruns the same suite with TSan.
not_done: Nothing from the package deliverable is missing. Deliberately outside the frozen headers / package text and therefore not emulated: CFData, CFSet, CFAllocator custom callbacks, CFDictionary/CFArray custom callbacks (the fake always uses CFType retain/release semantics), CMBlockBuffer custom block sources and non-contiguous sub-blocks, CMSampleBuffer multi-entry per-sample timing (only timing[0] is stored, as specified), CVPixelBuffer attributes/IOSurfaces/attachment APIs, and VideoToolbox decoder/session APIs other than the encoder object and the two session calls in n2vt_abi.h.
This is a host-only test double: there is no iOS build and no on-phone claim. It says nothing about the real Apple runtime except where the declared ABI is implemented.
The fake does not call baseClass->invalidate before finalize on release (the package text requires finalize; VCH263's invalidate slot is NULL).

commands.note: ASan+UBSan suite followed by the same suite rebuilt and run under TSan; both last lines are N2TEST WP02 PASS 10/10.
The acceptance compile command; zero warnings without -Werror.

commands.cmd: clang -std=c11 -O1 -g -Wall -Wextra -Werror -fsanitize=thread -DN2_HOST_FAKE -I gpu/video/include -I gpu/video/fake -pthread gpu/video/fake/fake_apple.c gpu/video/fake/fake_vt.c gpu/video/fake/test/t_fake.c -o gpu/video/build/WP02/tsan/t_fake && TSAN_OPTIONS=halt_on_error=1 gpu/video/build/WP02/tsan/t_fake

known_risks: CFDictionarySetValue on an existing key keeps the original key object and replaces only the value (it retains the new value and releases the old one); this follows Apple's documented CFDictionary behaviour but was not verified on the phone.

CMBlockBufferCreateWithMemoryBlock allocates eagerly whenever memoryBlock==NULL, ignoring blockAllocator, customBlockSource and deferred allocation. The package only requires the AssureMemoryNow path.

i420 chroma stride is round64(ceil(width/2)) (128 for 178) and the chroma plane has ceil(height/2) rows; only the 420v/420f stride rule was specified by the package, so the i420 choice is the fake's convention and is documented in the test.

CMVideoFormatDescriptionCreateFromH264ParameterSets checks that the first NAL is an SPS (type 7) but does not require the second to be a PPS (type 8), does not check forbidden_zero_bit, and does not parse the SPS. CoreMedia may be stricter; our callers always pass SPS then PPS.
CM object release calls finalize but not invalidate; no test currently depends on invalidate.
CFNumberGetValue from a double returns false for NaN and out-of-range values instead of saturating/rounding like some CoreFoundation builds; all callers in this tree use in-range values.

The intern table and its strings are process lifetime by design (not counted by n2fake_live_objects), so a test that expects a zero live count must take its baseline after its N2STR() calls; the live counter is for allocated CF objects, not interned names.

The n2fake_session struct itself is plain malloc, not a CF object, so it is not in the live-object count; the encoder, sample buffers and dictionaries created during a session are counted and are checked to return to the baseline.

Concurrent mutation of one CFDictionary/CFArray is not safe (as with real CF); the fake is thread-safe for refcounts, the intern table, the registry and independent objects, which is what WP05's two-session test uses.
